questions.question:
Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hard nut to crack

options.text: A situation that can be altered

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"****A problem difficult to solve."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expression** "hard nut to crack"** is an idiomatic phrase in English that means a difficult problem or a person who is not easy to understand, convince, or deal with. (कोई कठिन समस्या या ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसे समझना, समझाना या निपटना आसान नहीं है)
 
• It is often used to describe a challenging or formidable situation that requires a significant effort or skill to overcome.
 
 
• **Example**: *That math problem is a **hard nut to crack**__.*
 
 
 
• Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Sanyukta has to bake fifty-one cakes for the anniversary party.

options.text: Fifty-one cakes will be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
Fifty-one cakes had to be baken by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.
Fifty-one cakes has to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"****Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the active voice sentence, the subject is** "Sanyukta," **the verb is** "has to bake,"** and the object is **"fifty-one cakes for the anniversary party**."
 
• We must move the object to the beginning of the sentence and make it the new subject.
 
• We must add the original subject **("Sanyukta")** at the end with the preposition **"by"** to indicate the doer of the action in the passive voice.
 
• Structure__:
 __
 
• Subject + has/have + to + V1 + Object (Active Voice)__
 
• Object + has/have + to + be + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Disha has to arrange things. *(Active Voice)
 
• *Things have to be arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• We must use the past participle of the main verb ("bake") and add it to the new subject.
 
 
• Past participle of **"bake": baked**
 
• Passive verb phrase: **have to be baked**
 
 
 
• Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence: *Fifty-one cakes have to be baked by Sanyukta for the anniversary party.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

My father is reading the newspaper.

options.text: The newspaper is being read by my father.
The newspaper happens to be read by my father.
The newspaper was being read by my father.
My father likes reading the newspaper.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The newspaper is being read by my father."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **Present Continuous Tense **and in** Active Voice.**
 
• The rule for changing a **Present Continuous Tense** from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Structure: **
 
 
• **Subject + is/am/are + v1 + ing+ object (Active Voice)__**
 
• **Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by Subject __(Passive Voice)__ **
 
 
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *Esha is singing a song.** ***(Active Voice)**
 
• *A song is being sung by Esha.**** *(Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• **The subject** of the given sentence is **'My father.'​​**
 
• **The object** of the given sentence is** 'newspaper.' **
 
• **The subject** will be put in place of** the object **and** the object **will be put in place of **the subject.**
 
• And **'is reading** will be changed into **'is being read.' **
 
• **"Newspaper"** is a singular noun so we must **"is"** with it.
 
• "By my father" is added to indicate who is performing the action.
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
**Direction: The sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. The government's recent efforts have concentrated on strengthening these ties.

B. The textile industry in India is one of the country's oldest, stretching back several centuries.

C. The textile business is immensely diverse, with hand-spun and hand-woven textiles at one end of the spectrum and capital-intensive modern mills at the other.

D. Its tight ties to agriculture (for raw materials such as cotton) and the country's old history and traditions in terms of textiles set it apart from other sectors in the country.
questions.solution:

• **Sentence C**: Further elaborates on the diversity within the textile business, ranging from traditional hand-spun and hand-woven textiles to modern, capital-intensive mills.
 
• **Sentence D**: Expands on the unique characteristics of the textile industry in India, highlighting its ties to agriculture and its rich history and traditions.
 
• **Sentence A**: Concludes the paragraph by mentioning the government's recent efforts focused on strengthening ties related to the textile industry.
 
 
 
• The correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence:

B. The textile industry in India is one of the country's oldest, stretching back several centuries.

C. The textile business is immensely diverse, with hand-spun and hand-woven textiles at one end of the spectrum and capital-intensive modern mills at the other.

D. Its tight ties to agriculture (for raw materials such as cotton) and the country's old history and traditions in terms of textiles set it apart from other sectors in the country.

A. The government's recent efforts have concentrated on strengthening these ties.
